headerTitle: PSY632 — Theory and Practice of Counseling
subtitle: Midterm Important MCQs

mcqs.question: Burks & Stefflre (1979) define counseling as a professional relationship between whom?
options: A trained counselor and a client

mcqs.question: According to the BAC (1999) definition, the counselor offers the other person time, attention and respect to do what?
options: Explore, discover and clarify ways of living more resourcefully

mcqs.question: Rogers (1961) defined a helping relationship as one in which at least one party intends to promote what in the other?
options: Growth, development, maturity and improved coping with life

mcqs.question: Which characteristic of helping relationships means counselor and client share openly their perceptions and reactions?
In helping relationships, 'Privacy' means that:
options: All client disclosures during or after the session are confidential
The counselor shares disclosures with friends
Only the counselor's feelings are private

mcqs.question: Why is counseling NOT simply befriending, according to the handouts?
options: In friendship sharing is mutual, but in counseling sharing is one-sided

mcqs.question: Egan (1994) used which term to define a professional counselor?
According to Nelson-Jones (1997), the word 'helper' can place recipients in what position?
options: A dependent position, where the helper does things for rather than with the person

mcqs.question: Rogers (1957) identified which core conditions in the counseling relationship?
options: Empathy, unconditional positive regard and genuineness
Confidentiality, fees and time limits only

mcqs.question: Guidance is described in the handouts as:
options: An umbrella term including services for personal and career development and school adjustment

mcqs.question: What is a key distinction between guidance and counseling given in the handouts?
options: Guidance is between equals; counseling is between unequals only
Both focus only on the past
Guidance focuses on changes; counseling focuses only on choosing
Guidance focuses on helping individuals choose what they value most; counseling focuses on helping them make changes

mcqs.question: Brammer & Shostrom (1982) characterize counseling by which set of terms?
options: Focus on the past and severe emotional problems
Educational, vocational, supportive, situational, problem-solving, conscious awareness, normal, present time, short-term

mcqs.question: Counseling evolved from which movement, according to the handouts?
options: The human potential movements of the late 1950s and 1960s
The mental hygiene movement of 1909 only
Standardized testing in World War I

mcqs.question: Where are counselors more apt to work, compared with psychotherapists?
Which is a similarity between counseling and psychotherapy?
options: They differ in seating and have no common techniques
They use completely different ethical boundaries
Both value clients and build a special relationship, and use same theoretical models

mcqs.question: Who is rightly called the 'father of guidance'?
Who introduced the first general intelligence test in 1905 with Theodore Simon?
During World War I, the U.S. Army commissioned which intelligence tests for screening personnel?
Carl Rogers rose to prominence in 1942 with the publication of which book?
options: The Counselor in a Changing World

mcqs.question: Gerald Corey's early experience lesson shows that beginning counselors may:
options: Feel incompetent/inexperienced and expect clients to feel better quickly, learning clients need to struggle to find their own answers
Always feel fully confident from the start

mcqs.question: According to the handouts, what is the best rule of thumb for beginning clinicians regarding touching a client?
options: Refrain from the impulse to touch, especially early in the work with a client
Touch the client freely to show warmth from the first session
Touch only when the client is crying
Always touch the client's hand at the end of every session

mcqs.question: The two most important aspects of the use of space in counseling are:
Dissynchronous movement between counselor and client can indicate that:
options: The interview is on the wrong track
The client is ready for termination

mcqs.question: According to Fromm (1956), the word 'respect' comes from the Latin word 'respicere', meaning:
An accepting attitude toward clients means that the counselor:
options: Agrees with everything the client says
Judges the client's goodness or badness quickly
Suspends judgment on clients' goodness or badness and respects them as separate human beings with rights to their own thoughts and feelings
Ignores the client's version of reality

mcqs.question: Which of the following is listed as a barrier to an accepting attitude?
options: Trigger words, phrases and attitudes that raise a 'red flag' for the counselor

mcqs.question: Interpretation in counseling provides the client with:
options: A direct command about what action to take
An alternative frame of reference from which the client may view a situation
A summary of the counselor's own comments
Specific data on how others see the client

mcqs.question: A directive differs from advice/information in that a directive:
options: Is never used by behavioral counselors
Tells the client what action to take, and may be a simple suggestion stated in command form

mcqs.question: A client says she is nervous but smiles while saying it. This is an example of a mixed message involving:
options: Discrepancy between past and present statements
Discrepancy between words and actions at work
Discrepancy between verbal, voice and body messages

mcqs.question: When challenging a client, the counselor should:
options: Challenge the client persistently throughout every session
Raise their voice and point a finger for emphasis
Start by showing that they have heard and understood the client's messages, then build on this understanding with the challenging response

mcqs.question: The optimum distance between counselor and client found to be the average range of comfort is:
According to Strong (1968), the three characteristics of influential counselors are:
Transference is best described as:
options: The counselor's projected emotional reaction toward the client
The generalization of learning to daily life
The transfer of a client to another counselor at termination
The client's projection of past or present feelings, attitudes or desires onto the counselor

mcqs.question: Watkins (1985) identified four forms of countertransference. Which set is correct?
Frank Parsons founded the Vocational Bureau in Boston in which year and wrote 'Choosing a Vocation' in which year?
Parsons suggested three factors important for wise selection of a vocation. Which is one of them?
options: Extensive self-study on a Schedule of personal data

mcqs.question: Jesse B. Davis is associated with what early contribution?
options: Founding the National Committee for Mental Hygiene
Writing A Mind That Found Itself
Introducing vocational and moral guidance as curriculum / first systematic guidance program in public schools

mcqs.question: Clifford Beers exposed conditions in mental institutions in which book (1908)?
Williamson's approach in the 1930s is described as:
The National Defense Education Act (NDEA) of 1958 did what?
options: Provided funds to strengthen school guidance programs and train school counselors

mcqs.question: The National Board for Certified Counselors (NBCC) was formed in which year?
In 1992, AACD changed its name to what?
According to the handouts, counseling is NOT a value-free or neutral activity. Who is cited for this (1992)?
Meier and Davis (2001) principles for effective helpers include:
options: Hide behind too many tests and avoid supervision
Become aware of personal issues, be open to supervision, avoid hiding behind too many tests, consult on ethical dilemma

mcqs.question: Jahoda (1958) proposed criteria for mental health including:
options: Positive attitude toward self, movement toward self-actualization, purpose in life, independent functioning, accurate perception of reality, mastery of environment
Dependence on others and avoidance of purpose

mcqs.question: According to Krumboltz (1965), counseling is an effort to help the client engage in behavior that will lead to what?
options: A resolution of the client's problems
A complete change of basic character structure

mcqs.question: Blocher (1966) described the goals of counseling as ordinarily:
According to Blocher (1966), counseling clients are viewed as:
options: Capable of choosing goals, making decisions and assuming responsibility for their behavior
Always in need of long-term treatment

mcqs.question: According to Blocher, counseling focuses mainly on:
Krumboltz (1966) criteria for judging counseling goals include which?
options: Goals capable of being stated differently for each client, compatible with counselor values, and degree of attainment observable
Goals must be identical for every client

mcqs.question: Which is listed as a major goal of counseling?
Ethics are defined as:
options: Suggested standards of conduct based on a consensus value set

mcqs.question: Which is listed as unethical behavior in counseling?
options: Violation of confidentiality and imposing one's values on a client

mcqs.question: Informed consent involves:
options: A one-time verbal agreement only at termination
Client rights to be informed about what the relationship will entail and to make autonomous decisions, starting with intake interview

mcqs.question: Which is a stated limitation of confidentiality?
options: Suspected child abuse must be reported and threats to harm others must be reported

mcqs.question: The Tarasoff case (1969) is a famous example of:
options: Duty to warn - failure to notify an intended victim of a threat resulting in murder

mcqs.question: A dual relationship refers to:
options: Professional assuming two or more roles simultaneously or sequentially with person seeking help, e.g. friendship and business deals
Seeing two clients in group work

mcqs.question: Bartering in counseling is:
options: Practice of counseling for goods or other services, e.g. cleaning house or secretarial service
Referring a client to another agency

mcqs.question: Herlihy and Corey guidelines for dealing with dual relationship issues include:
options: Hide the relationship and avoid documentation
Secure informed consent, seek consultation, document and monitor, obtain supervision

mcqs.question: In promoting decision making, what is the counselor's role?
options: Counselor makes decisions for the client
Counselor just promotes, not makes, decisions; provides information and clarifies characteristics and emotions
Counselor decides based on test scores only

mcqs.question: Empathy, as described by Rogers, is best defined as:
options: Feeling sorry for the sufferer, as in sympathy
Seeing the world through another's eyes, feeling and experiencing their internal world / viewing through another's frame of reference
Mixing counselor's thoughts and feelings with client's

mcqs.question: Positive regard can be defined as:
options: Being able to recognize values and strengths in clients even when client holds widely different attitudes
Supporting every behavior of the client

mcqs.question: Congruence or genuineness is defined as:
options: Complete openness that may damage client at all times
Consistency in values, attitudes and behaviors on part of counselor; being authentic and real

mcqs.question: Combs et al. (1969) concluded effective helpers perceive others as:
options: Able, dependable, friendly, worthy and able to cope and be self-disclosing
Unable to solve their own problems

mcqs.question: Which is listed as a HARMFUL motive for entering counseling profession?
options: Unresolved emotional pain, do-gooding and seeking intimacy

mcqs.question: Belkin (1984) suggests the primary value counselors must commit themselves to is:
Rogers (1961) described empathy as the ability to enter the client's phenomenological world and experience it:
options: Exactly as your own, losing your own identity completely
As if it were your own without ever losing the 'as if' quality
From a completely detached, external viewpoint
Only through the client's written reports

mcqs.question: Advanced empathy differs from primary empathy in that advanced empathy:
options: Only restates the client's exact words
Explores themes, issues, meanings and emotions that are below the surface of what is being shared
Is used only in the first session

mcqs.question: Attacking questions must be eradicated from the counselor's repertoire because they:
options: Serve to shame the client or demonstrate the counselor's power over the client

mcqs.question: Microskills in counseling are defined as:
options: Observable actions of counselors and therapists that appear to effect positive change in the session

mcqs.question: Attending skills in counseling refer to:
options: Focused attention placed on the other person in an interchange between two or more people

mcqs.question: In nonverbal communication, 'timing' refers to:
options: Only the total length of the counseling contract
The counselor's speed of taking notes
All time parameters of the session, such as starting and ending on time and the use of time within sessions
The client's age and developmental stage

mcqs.question: Congruence in nonverbal communication refers to the clinician's efforts to:
options: Match the client's posture at all times
Keep personal verbal and nonverbal expressions in line with each other
Speak in the same accent as the client

mcqs.question: Sensitivity, as a concept facilitating good nonverbal communication, refers to:
options: The client's sensitivity to the counselor's feelings
The provider's ability to receive and understand the client's nonverbal communications
Avoiding eye contact with shy clients

mcqs.question: Synchrony refers to the clinician's ability to:
options: Schedule sessions at the same time each week
End the session exactly on time
Take notes in rhythm with the client's speech
Match or oppose the client's nonverbal expressions as therapeutically indicated

mcqs.question: A client talks anxiously about wanting to run when she saw a friend while shopping. Which response shows the counselor staying on the topic (attending)?
options: 'Did you get admission in bachelors this year?'
'You say you wanted to run when you saw your friend. Can you describe the situation in more detail?'
'Let us talk about your childhood instead.'

mcqs.question: To convey patience nonverbally, the counselor should use:
options: Folded arms and a stern expression
Slow rate of speech, patient gestures and focused attention

mcqs.question: The term 'active listening' was popularized by Thomas Gordon in his 1970 book:
What is the distinction between hearing and listening given in the handouts?
options: Hearing involves accurately understanding meaning; listening is only receiving sound
Hearing involves the capacity to be aware of and receive sound; listening also involves accurately understanding their meaning
There is no distinction between them
Listening is a passive process; hearing is an active process

mcqs.question: The first prerequisite to complete and active listening is the ability to:
options: Interrupt the client to ask clarifying questions frequently
Summarize after every sentence the client speaks
Allow a client to speak uninterruptedly, even if the client takes breaks or pauses

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an importance of active listening mentioned in the handouts?
options: It helps clients to assume responsibility for working on their problems
It allows the counselor to give advice more quickly
It eliminates the need for structure in counseling
It guarantees the client will change immediately

mcqs.question: Suggestive questions are problematic because they:
options: Put the client on the defensive by shaming them
Give hidden (or not so hidden) advice disguised as a question

mcqs.question: Questions such as 'But you aren't taking drugs yourself?' are examples of:
options: Assumptive questions, which give the impression the counselor expects a particular answer

mcqs.question: Why have questions starting with 'why' fallen into disregard among counselors?
options: They are too difficult to phrase
They take too long to answer
Judgmental questions such as 'Why did you do that?' put the client on the defensive or create discomfort

mcqs.question: Closed questions can be used purposefully in which situation?
options: During a crisis situation or when a client is excessively anxious
When the counselor wants rich self-disclosure
When building initial rapport over several sessions

mcqs.question: In open-ended questions, the word 'How' is used to ask about:
Paraphrasing means:
options: Repeating the client's words exactly like a parrot in every response
Rewording the speaker's verbal utterances to repeat back the essence of the client's words and thoughts, to check the clarity of the counselor's understanding

mcqs.question: A tip for good paraphrasing given in the handouts is to:
options: Start your responses with the personal pronoun 'you' to indicate that you reflect the client's internal viewpoint

mcqs.question: Reflecting feelings differs from paraphrasing in that reflecting feelings:
options: Is simple mirroring of words only
Is concerned with feelings and emotions, responding to clients' 'music' and not just their words
Is used only at the end of counseling

mcqs.question: When reflecting feelings, the counselor should mirror the intensity of the client's feeling words. 'Devastated' indicates:
Summaries in counseling are used to:
options: Pull together material in a counseling session over a period of time and provide structure to a casual random conversation

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a type of summary listed in the handouts?
options: Diagnostic summary made without the client
Basic reflection summary, which can take place at any stage of counseling
Summary given only by the client

mcqs.question: The Basic Listening Sequence (BLS) consists of:
options: Interpretation, directive, advice, feedback and logical consequences
Open questions, closed questions, encouragement, paraphrasing, reflection of feeling and summarization
Rapport, goal setting and termination only

mcqs.question: Which skills are classified as influencing skills in the handouts?
options: Interpretation/reframing, directive, advice/information, self-disclosure, feedback, logical consequences and influencing summary

mcqs.question: Feedback as an influencing skill provides clients with:
options: The logical consequences of their actions
A new interpretation of their childhood
Specific data on how they are seen by the counselor or by others

mcqs.question: Logical consequences as an influencing skill is most frequently employed by:
Regarding focusing, the handouts advise that it is generally wiser to:
options: Focus on the problem first and ignore the person
Focus only on the family from the start
First focus on the client and later on the problem
Avoid focusing on the client altogether

mcqs.question: Which of the following is one of the seven dimensions of microskill focus analysis?
Egan (1994) defined challenge/confrontation as:
options: An invitation to examine internal or external behavior that seems to be self-defeating, harmful to others, or both — and to change that behavior
A hostile and aggressive act against the client
A technique for ending counseling quickly

mcqs.question: According to Shulman (1979), how much of the time in a counseling relationship should be devoted to focusing on termination?
options: One-sixth of the time — e.g. 3 sessions out of 18

mcqs.question: How do counseling and psychotherapy differ in duration and sessions?
options: Counseling is unlimited; psychotherapy is 1 session
Counseling usually 6-12 sessions and less than 6 months; psychotherapy 20-40 sessions over 6 months to 2 years
Counseling 20-40 sessions over 2 years; psychotherapy 6-12 sessions
Both always last more than 2 years

mcqs.question: An important self-disclosure made a few minutes before the end of a session may communicate:
options: That the client has fully resolved the issue
That the counselor should cancel the next session
Ambivalence on the client's part about whether to discuss the topic

mcqs.question: In the counseling process, 'structure' refers to:
options: The joint understanding between counselor and client regarding the characteristics, conditions, procedures and parameters of counseling
The physical layout of the counseling room only

mcqs.question: In the first stage of counseling, two struggles take place: the battle for structure and the battle for initiative. It is important that:
options: The counselor wins the battle for structure and the client wins the battle for initiative

mcqs.question: Resistance in counseling is best defined as:
options: Unwillingness to change; resistant clients cling to the certainty of the present and do not want to face the pain that change demands

mcqs.question: Otani (1988) categorized forms of resistance into four broad categories. Which is one of them?
options: Amount of verbalization, shown by silence and minimum talk
The physical setting of the room

mcqs.question: The five stages of the interview structure, in order, begin with rapport and structure and end with:
options: Generalizing and transferring learning to daily life

mcqs.question: Resistances may be broadly defined as:
options: Only the client's refusal to pay fees
Anything that gets in the way of counseling, and they can be present at any stage of counseling
Problems that occur only at termination

mcqs.question: One way to deal with initial resistances is to 'join with clients', which means:
options: Agreeing that counseling is a waste of time and ending it
Confronting the client aggressively in the first session
Showing clients that you understand their internal viewpoints, e.g. reflecting a client's anger about coming because his parents are the ones with problems
Involving the client's parents in every session

mcqs.question: A formal termination of counseling serves three functions. Which is one of them?
options: It transfers the client's problems to the counselor
It allows the counselor to extend the relationship indefinitely
It signals that something is finished and serves as a reminder that the client has matured
It tests the client's memory of the sessions
